SH-CORE-07 T1 / SH-EXP-09 / SH-USER-01: run the echo -e/-n tell on #!/bin/sh files only (1920 hits, 4 in MUST scope) and drop the echo -e alternative from u01.
SH-ERR-03 G-IFS: match only a line that is the global IFS=$'..' assignment (80% of hits were while-read, local or prefix forms).
SH-GATE-02 cell 02-c: four keys, matching X51; the printed five-key cell flags every compliant rc.
SH-DIAL-06 d06: require bash shapes for [-N], skip balanced quotes for |& and &>>, and filter bats titles, BASH_VERSINFO guards and ${VAR:-} probes (26% FP).

surprises: A trap RETURN set inside a bash function persists after it returns and re-fires on later source/dot (and every function under set -T), but NOT on plain later function calls on bash 3.2-5.3; a stale single-quoted rm -rf trap deleted a reused variable's directory. dokku has 44 such traps and zero resets. New class SH-ERR-34.

The SH-CORE-07 T1 / SH-EXP-09 / u01 echo -e cell is 99.8% outside MUST scope (1916 of 1920 hits; LinuxGSM alone 1159); echo "$var", which the rule bans, appears 2073 times in the same 16 trees, so only a reading heuristic can enforce it.
Listing-cell noise dominates: G-IFS 80% false, s05 94%, X08 74%, G-ERRTRAP 73%, d06 26% (30 of 36 from OpenWrt UCI @device[-1] paths); every one was fixed with a plant/twin pair.

The gate-of-record script itself misses '#! /bin/sh' (space after the bang): a non-ASCII file passes with rc 0. pfetch is valid UTF-8 and still fails to parse under yash 2.52 in the C locale, so the ASCII rule is right and the detection was wrong.

SH-ERR-31 in the wild: only 1 of 59 guards includes the -L form; 63 of 98 unguarded loops are repo-internal (non-empty by construction); void-packages tests [ -z "${#a[@]}" ] on a glob array, which can never fire (max=1 on 8 bash versions).

ShellCheck 0.11.0 reports SC2218 as an error on bats helpers defined below the @test that calls them, though bats evaluates the whole file first and the tests pass. SH-GATE-07 has no row for it; the fix is ordering, not a disable.

top_rules: Build every emitted value with one per-shell quoter; never Rust {:?}, Go %q or a bare "%s" template (fnm/vfox/carapace fail 21-26 of 33-34 corpus cases; check C5 plant 5 hits, twin 0).

PowerShell single-quote quoters must double U+2018-U+201B as well as the apostrophe; U+2018 help text executes on pwsh 7.4.7, 7.6.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (exit 1 3/3; fixed and ASCII twins green).
Emit executable paths into pwsh as & '<doubled-quote path>', never inside double quotes (vfox) and never undoubled in single quotes (mcfly): 21/34 and 23/34 corpus cases fail.
Bash hooks must append to an array PROMPT_COMMAND or fall back to a string below bash 5.1; vfox's prepend loses the user's hook on bash 3.2-5.0 (5 of 40 scenarios red).
A hook matrix with zero firings is invalid, and tty-gated emitters (mcfly bash) must be driven on a pty: pipe-fed run was 40/40 blind, pty run measured 0/25 failing.
Judge fish hooks per event (fish_postexec vs fish_prompt) and treat an empty docker-pty row as INVALID, never as a pass.
fish files that must run below 4.7.0 never put an unknown command left of ||; 3.6.0 and 4.0.2 skip the RHS (check F5b, plant 2, twin 0).
elvish: never write NAME=value cmd (removed in 0.21.0, compiles clean, fails at run time); use tmp or with (check E2b, plant 1, twin 0; elvish-modules git-vcsh.elv:26 is a true hit).
Run nu gates on modules through a use DIR/ wrapper and declare a nu floor; nupm is 13/25 red unwrapped and clean wrapped on 0.116.1.
Harnesses that run third-party installers must scrub the environment with env -i (broot --install honours an inherited ZDOTDIR and wrote to the real ~/.zshrc).

top_rules: Verdict: SH-TEST is not clean on held-out suites; the census and L2, L3, L5, L6, P1, P2 and Test-DiscoveryCode need amendments, rule IDs stay.

Census must consult the bats exit status and require result lines equal to the TAP plan, no duplicate numbers and no '# bats warning' line; a plan-only census was green on a 0-of-2 run and on Bash-it 255-of-308.
Every file calling bats_test_function needs a pin 'N path' and 'bats --count FILE' must equal N; static grep false-reds dynamic suites and stays green when a generator input vanishes.

Never count with 'bats --count -r DIR': it runs top-level code, descends into vendored submodules (basher 429 vs 138) and counts fixture .bats (bats-file 227 vs 212); keep the git ls-files static grep with CENSUS_EXCLUDE.
Never gate on '--formatter junit' stdout (no TAP plan); use --report-formatter junit --output beside TAP, or the junit census (sum tests= equals bats --count).

No '|| true' directly after an assertion and no mid-test [[ ]] without '|| return 1': l2v3 (plant red, twin green, corpus 0 vs 200 false hits) and l3v2 (10 bats-assert sites green on bash 3.2.57, red on 5.3.20).

Ban disabled-test forms: commented-out '# @test' (39 in asdf, nodenv, dokku) and 'skip' as a test's first statement (dokku 1, Bash-it 2); also every .bats must be run by the gate (asdf Go harness omits 9 files and comments out 1).

Gate Pester on TotalCount>0, skipped budget, all three failed counters and Result, and pin the total for generated suites (-ExpectedTotal); the Pode, PSDepend and dbatools forms all stay green on zero-test and skip-only runs, and scan *.tests.ps1 case-insensitively.
surprises: bats-assert has 10 mutation-proven vacuous '[[ =~ ]]' assertions: a never-matching pattern gives exit 0 on bash 3.2.57 and exit 1 on 5.3.20.

The original census exits 0 on a bats 1.14.0 run without GNU parallel that executed 0 of 2 tests, and on a Bash-it --tap --jobs 4 run that lost 53 of 308 result lines (bats itself exited 1 with a warning).

asdf's Go harness hand-lists bats files: 9 of 32 are never run and version_commands.bats (63 tests) is commented out, so a directory census describes tests CI does not execute; bats-mock's npm test is 'echo todo'.

Test-DiscoveryCode v1 was wrong 114 of 116 times on Pode, dbatools and PSDepend (InModuleScope wrappers and -ForEach data); my first l2v2 revision also missed '[ "$status" -eq 1 ] || true' because it forbade quotes.

Pester 6 -AllowNullOrEmptyForEach silently empties a Describe over an empty generator while every exit-code gate stays green; Pester 5.9.1 does the same without the flag (total=1); and pester-lint P2 never scans lowercase *.tests.ps1 files that Pester does run.

bats --jobs result loss showed up on 1.11.1 and 1.14.0 (3 of 4 Bash-it runs, under host load ~100) but not on 9 bats-assert runs; the two identical 255-line truncations are unexplained, so the round only proves the exit-code and warning gate, not a root cause.

top_rules: SH-SEC-02 AMEND (MUST): a secret reaches no argv by any route (variable, array, set --, read -s, docker -e K=V, --build-arg, cargo --token); new MUST cell checks/secret-argv.sh, waiver # sec-ok:, exit map 0/1/69/74/78/79, plant 18 / twin 0 on five hosts and three awks.

SH-SEC-09 AMEND (MUST): validate a data-valued name before any name-taking construct on every shell, not only bash; the bash-only safe list (export, readonly, unset) is withdrawn; cell s09r supersedes the old listing.

SH-SEC-13 NEW (MUST): git credentials never ride a userinfo URL, git -c http.extraheader or a persistent http.extraHeader; use GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 env on the one command (git 2.31+), a GIT_ASKPASS script reading a 0600 file, or credential.helper store.
SH-SEC-14 NEW (MUST): cargo --token is argv; use CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN for crates.io only and CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN for any other registry, or cargo login on stdin.
Never name a secret custom header and enable GIT_TRACE_CURL: it redacts Authorization, cookies and Proxy-Authorization only; an X-Token header printed the token 5 times on three git versions.

git -c http.extraheader is worse than the env form: the parent argv holds the token and the children also carry it in environ (GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS); a userinfo URL is argv in three processes plus .git/config.

Gate hand-off (SH-GATE-09/22): shfmt -f must be shfmt -f -- with stderr captured and exit 74; a tracked file named -x.sh makes shfmt fail, and a gate that discards stderr reads it as an empty list and passes.
Waive git's own fake-credential test lines with # sec-ok: test credential; 11 of the 71 corpus findings are git t/ fixtures that are true to the pattern but not real secrets.
surprises: CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN does nothing for an alternative registry: exit 101 'no token found for stub' on cargo 1.93.1, 1.94.0, 1.95.0 and 1.99.0, even with CARGO_REGISTRY_DEFAULT=stub; only CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN works.

SH-SEC-09 is not bash-specific: mksh R59c and posh 0.14.1 execute a[$(cmd)] through local, typeset, export, readonly, unset and read; zsh 5.0.8 to 5.9 through export and read (printf -v from 5.3.1); dash, busybox ash 1.35/1.37, ksh93u+m 2023/1.0.10 and yash 2.52 never did. The old 'safe on all eight: export, readonly, unset' list is a bash-only fact.

The check finds 26 of 71 corpus findings and 32 of 80 held-out findings that the existing single-line s02-argv grep cannot see (neither the use line nor the taint line matches), and the fleet has 8 variable-carried or direct sources in 7 repos, not the 4 recorded in wave 3.

docker run -e K=V (jdx/mise registry-impl.yml:251, cli/cli run.sh:104) is a production leak shape not in the wave-3 rule: the value is in the docker client argv; -e K with an env prefix or --secret id=,env= fixes it.

GIT_TRACE_CURL redaction is by header name: Authorization was redacted (0 leaks) but a custom X-Token header printed the token 5 times; git -c puts the token in children's environ as well as the parent argv.

A gate that swallows shfmt stderr turns a dash-leading tracked file (-x.sh) into an empty file list and exit 0; shfmt -f -- was watched red (variant exits 74) and green; the held-out set stopped being held-out after its false positives were fixed, the unseen 7-repo round (5 of 5 true) is the clean one.

rule_ids: SH-SEC-01 — Fix the five injection ShellCheck findings (SC2254, SC2053, SC2295, SC2035, SC2156) and never disable them; any per-site disable carries a same-line reason.

SH-SEC-02 — Never put a secret on a command line by any route (literal, variable, array, set --, read -s, docker run -e K=V, --build-arg, cargo --token, userinfo URL); use stdin, then a 0600 file, then the one-command environment.
SH-SEC-03 — Do not enable xtrace in a file that expands a secret; bracket the secret line with { set +x; } 2>/dev/null.
SH-SEC-04 — Never give PATH an empty, . or relative entry; extend it as PATH="$d${PATH:+:$PATH}" and pin it when privileged.
